outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Efficient Finetuning of Large Language Models
outline.description: Sets the stage by discussing why finetuning large models is important, the memory challenges involved, and the high‑level idea behind QLoRA.
subtopics: Motivation for finetuning LLMs
Memory bottlenecks of standard 16‑bit finetuning
Limitations of existing quantization methods for training
Overview of QLoRA and its goals

outline.description: Reviews the technical foundations required to understand QLoRA: quantization basics, block‑wise k‑bit quantization, and Low‑Rank Adaptation (LoRA).
subtopics: Quantization: definitions, scaling, and dequantization
Block‑wise k‑bit quantization and outlier handling
Low‑Rank Adapter (LoRA) formulation
Memory profile of PEFT methods (activations vs. adapter parameters)
Why LoRA alone does not solve the memory problem

outline.description: Detailed presentation of the three novel components that make QLoRA possible.
subtopics: 4‑bit NormalFloat (NF4) data type – theory and construction
Double Quantization of scale constants – algorithm and memory impact
Paged Optimizers using NVIDIA unified memory – handling optimizer state spikes
Interaction of storage vs. compute data types (NF4 ↔ BF16)
Full forward/backward pass through quantized weights

outline.description: Mathematical formalism of QLoRA for a single layer and the end‑to‑end finetuning pipeline.
subtopics: Notation for quantized weight tensor, scales, and LoRA matrices
Double dequantization formula
"Dequant → compute → re‑quant" workflow per forward pass
Gradient flow: why only LoRA gradients are needed
Algorithmic steps: loading, dequantizing, forward, loss, backward, optimizer update

outline.description: Covers engineering choices that make large‑scale QLoRA feasible on a single GPU.
subtopics: Choice of block size for weights (64) and scale constants (256)
"Paged" optimizer configuration in PyTorch/Accelerate
Integration with bitsandbytes and HuggingFace Transformers
CUDA kernels for NF4 de/quantization
Training hyperparameters (learning rate schedules, batch sizes) across model scales
